temperature_range: 443 K to 723 K for precursor deposition, 398 K to 623 K for reduction
summary: The study describes the preparation of Cu/Pd bimetallic nanoparticle catalysts using atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) on SiO2 and γ-Al2O3 supports. The ALE process involves sequential deposition of copper and palladium precursors, followed by thermal treatment. EXAFS and TEM analyses reveal alloying behavior, with surface segregation observed on silica-supported samples and random alloying on alumina-supported samples. The process enables highly dispersed metal oxides and facilitates alloy formation, which can enhance catalytic properties.
evidence: The ALE samples were prepared by sequential deposition of Cu(thd)2 and Pd(thd)2 at 443 K and 723 K, respectively. The reduction temperature ranged from 398 K to 623 K. EXAFS and TEM analyses showed alloying with surface segregation on silica and random alloying on alumina. The study highlights the formation of Cu/Pd alloys through ALE, which can improve catalytic performance.
